title: Silence and the Peace of the Triad
english: Having conquered suffering, he who claims to possess virtue unassailed is still passion-driven; for against the battle-array of the virtuous strategy of labors, the vice of the adversaries is also drawn up in counter-formation. It has been taken away for a heart without war to be in virtue. For virtue is called a practical name from deeds of valor. Virtue does not seek the praises of men, for it takes no delight in honor, the mother of evils. The beginning of honor is people-pleasing, and its end is pride. For he who demands honors exalts himself, and such a one does not know how to bear being made nothing; the desire for honor is a fantasy, for he who loves it fantasizes about its inheritance.

Let the labor of the virtues be honor to you, and dishonor be praise according to human will; seek no glory from the flesh, O you who destroy the passions of the flesh, but seek the better thing, and glory shall be yours. He who wishes to be honored envies the one who is approved. And he who is defeated by excessive honors heaps hatred upon jealousy toward him; he wishes no one to be preferred before himself, but snatches the first places, lest he appear inferior; he cannot bear to honor the approved man in his absence, but even in his own labors he mocks the low-seeking glory, and insolence is a most sharp slaughter to the glory-seeker, and he does not entirely escape wrath from this.

Chapter 4. Such a person serves a barbarian mistress and was sold to many masters — to pride, envy, jealousy, and the aforesaid picked troops of the spirits; but he who shatters the spirit of honor by humility will utterly destroy the whole legion of demons. He who makes himself a slave to all through humility will be conformed to the one who humbled himself, having received the form of a slave. If you measure yourself by the smallest measure, you will not measure yourself against a companion, and he who reveals the weakness of the soul through lamentations will not think much of those laboring upon themselves.

Demons bring vileness and insolence upon the humble-minded, so that, not bearing their own nothingness, they may flee from humility; but he who bravely bears dishonors through humility is raised by them all the more to the height of philosophy. David, being insulted, did not answer back, but even checked the vengeance of Abishai. And you, being insulted, do not insult in return, but rightly calm the one avenging you; bear insolence — your own progress — and with lips close the door of thumos; you will answer those who threaten not at all, so that by silence you may lull the smoking lips; you will pain those who then threaten and insult when you put bridles on your jaws. For you, by being silent, will not be consumed by insult, but he is all the more bitten by your silence, if you long-sufferingly endure the insolence of the insolent; shake off the praise of men from within, so that you may shake off the ostentatious thought before it.

And watch also for self-satisfaction, especially in stillness, lest having magnified yourself above the insolent one, you dishonor him. One of the brothers was insulted by a pious one, and having endured injustice, he departed divided between joy and grief: partly because, being wronged, he was insulted and was not provoked in return, and partly because the pious one was deceived and, having deceived, rejoiced. But consider for me also the deceiver, having suffered both: in that he disturbed, he wholly rejoiced at having disturbed, and in that he was not provoked in return, he was more grieved.

Chapter 5. When the demons see us not inflamed unto the same grating of insults, then, standing by in stillness, they pry up the ruling faculty, so that those with whom, being present, we made peace, when they depart we may speak boldly against. Therefore, if you carry out a dispute or an insult toward a brother, consider yourself to have failed, so that in stillness you may not find a battle of thoughts in your heart, one reproaching the manner of the insults, and the other reproaching in return that the terrible things happened and you did not insult in return. When a provocation embitters the brothers in the community, then the thoughts cast in to call the solitary blessed, so that, having emptied us of long-suffering, they may separate us from love. But he who overturns anger with long-suffering, and grief with love, overturns two evil beasts with twofold manliness, fighting with thumos; he who exhorts, and falls on his knees, so that he may drive away anger, drives both the provoker and the provoked away from himself, because he who makes peace among the angry wages war against the spirit of anger; but the anger of kinsmen will rage against him for his insolence toward him, because he took the fight of his neighbors upon himself — he who bears the impudence for the sake of peace is compelled to become a son of peace; but the bond of peace is to be sought not only toward men, but also in your body, and in your spirit, and in your soul.

title: The Nature of Sorrow and Endurance
english: In peace, then, as being united by the commandment of the Divine Trinity, you hear: 'Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called sons of God' (Matt 5:9). For if you bring the flesh, which is contrary to the desire of the spirit, into peace through labors, you shall gain glory among the beatitudes beyond this age, having conquered the war in your body that fights against the law of your mind and captures you by the law of sin in your members.

Great is the bond of peace, in which also the joy that enlightens the eye of the intellect for the contemplation of the higher powers is united; if, therefore, we might acquire the peaceful joy in the midst of labors, we would thankfully repel the difficult things that come upon us through it, and we would not admit the demon of sorrow who, especially by mutilating in tribulations, falls upon the soul, and prepares a space of acedia so that they may darken the soul and at the same time stir up pains. Let the joy of peace, therefore, be a written law of our heart, drowning sorrow, driving out hatred, destroying anger, dissolving acedia, and compensating for grief. For it is a sea of virtues, nestling in peaceful patience, in thanksgiving, and in endurance, drowning the opposition of the devil by the cross.

But consider for me the opposing joy standing near in turmoil, lest, shadowed, you be deceived into grasping one kind instead of another. For the demons also fashion themselves after the spiritual gifts, so that, having led the mind astray by the overshadowing, they may remove it from its wits; for a spiritual joy stands near the heart when nothing is present, because it finds the ruler hanging aloft, away from godly sorrow, but later it delivers the soul to the Spirit of sorrow, because it made it captive of spiritual joy.

CHAPTER 7. I say this too, as the experience of those seeking has suggested to one of the brothers, that instead of rejoicing in the Lord (Phil 4:4), the avenger brings in a domestic joy against [it]. And instead of godly sorrow, he treacherously brings the opposite upon the mind, so that the soul may be darkened by anxieties over the shifting changes of the ray of the superior ones. Sorrows are twofold, being yoked to every work of evil, and...

One sorrow stands by the heart from an unseen cause, while another is born, driven by different causes; the sorrow according to God calls the soul back through tears, not accepting either opposing joy or sorrow, and being anxious about the approaching death and judgment; and this has gaped, awaiting little by little.

Failed desires plant sorrows; but prayers and thanksgivings wither these; between angry persons a middle sorrow trembles. Therefore, the first one, having sobered up, if he rises from the passion and gives his hand to the other, by apology drives away the bitter sorrow. Sorrow is a disease of soul and flesh; it lifts up the captive woman and withers the one upon the spot. From opposites sorrow is born, and from sorrow wrath, and from these is born phrenitis — reviling. If you wish to trample together sorrow and wrath, embrace the long-suffering of love and clothe yourself in the joy of harmlessness; let your joy not be sorrow to another; he who rejoices in injustice will mourn in prosperity, and he who endures, suffering unjustly, will shine with exultation; for the things to come are contrary to the things present.

Chapter 8. In tribulations be most thankful, because through them you will more clearly perceive the grace of assistance. For thus, thankfully shaking off the coming tribulations, you will not dim the most brilliant beauty of patience, even if a demon lashes you according to the flesh — he will be found a procurer of the greatest reward for you, if you receive the wound on the subject of thanksgiving. For thus you will put even him to flight from you. And so that your reward may rain down more through endurance, let your endurance act as general through the pursuit of courageous labors; for through every evil, acedia also counter-attacks you, and spying upon all your labors, it tempts; whomever it does not find nailed by endurance, him it weighs down under itself and bends low; but if the demon of acedia grows weak against the endurance of labors, the beast again bites the achievement of despair; if then with understanding you drive this away, you will also drive the vainglorious spirit in him at the time of gathering. title: The Meekness of the Combatant
english: A memory, as if having been exhausted for some reason. Therefore, when we are awake at night, let us not incline the assembly toward acedia, so that the demons, standing by, do not gather the tares of the thoughts and sow them together in the heart; for when we destroy the assembly of hymns, then we gather together the assembly of thoughts. Having been awakened before the assembly, let us practice thoughts of light in the heart beforehand, so that, having been made ready, we may stand at the psalmody with a watchful mind.

In one way the psalm must be said with a rushing sound in wakefulness, in another way one must be tested against babbling in the psalmody; for according to the ambush of the adversary it is necessary that we also be transformed, because at times they suggest letting the tongue run, the soul being held by acedia, and at times they provoke the words to be sung, just as the noetic eye receives its strength from the food of light. For he who stretches himself toward the vision of the high things will receive a sharper eye, according to the pattern of Elisha (2 Kings 6:17).

When a thought comes as an enemy to your heart, do not seek other things instead of others through prayer, but whet the sword of tears against the enemy; for in this way, if we strike more fiercely in the battle, we will make him depart from us more readily. Love beauty with the work of the hands, and especially the memory of prayer; for the one is not always, but the other, unceasing, has the means of the labor.

Do not hesitate to give the debt of prayer, hearing a thought through the pretext of works, and do not cause turmoil in the work, tossing the body about, so that you may not disturb the heart of prayer together with it. Just as the outer man works with hands so as not to burden anyone, so let the one in the thoughts work, so that the mind may not be burdened. For the thoughts bring their own work to the soul when they catch it idle with respect to godly thoughts.

O unplowed field: let the works of the hands be toward love of mankind, and the mind of the rational part toward love of wisdom, so that the one may be a hospitality to strangers and a burning of laziness, but the other a general of contemplation and a shaking-off of thoughts; let us strike the pleasures of the thoughts with boldness, turning all our anger toward them, so that we do not, by receiving things from them through pleasure, become gentle toward them in return.

Chapter 10. Prepare yourself to be both meek and a combatant, the one toward your kinsman and the other toward the enemy; for in this is the use of thumos, in opposing the serpent according to enmity; and in this is the reasonableness of meekness, in being long-suffering toward the brother according to love, and fighting against the thought. Let the meek man, therefore, be a combatant, meekness being divided from the deceitful thoughts, just as battle is divided from those of the same nature; do not turn the use of thumos toward the life contrary to nature, so as to be angry at the brother according to the likeness of the serpent, but to be befriended by the serpent according to the agreement of the thoughts. The meek man, even if he suffers terrible things, does not depart from love; for because of this he is long-suffering and endures, he is kind and remains. For if long-suffering belongs to love, thumos-fighting does not belong to love; for thumos stirs up grief and wrath, but love diminishes these three things. If you have a firm foundation in love, attend more to this than to what afflicts you; serve God in fear and in love, the one as Master and Judge, the other as Lover of mankind, and He nourishes. He who has acquired the virtues of love takes captive the passions of the wicked, and he who has these three things from the Holy Trinity — faith, hope, love — will be a city fortified by a triple wall for the virtues. You will be revealed as loving not only in not receiving from another, but in giving ungrudgingly as one who has renounced, in giving, as you struggle with matter, to cast pure seeds, so that instead of wheat, nettle does not come forth to you. Remember God in the things you provide, both giver and receiver, so that He may reckon to you the wages of your renunciation along with praises.

Chapter 11. The unattached man has the pleasure of life without care, but the lover of possessions has the pain of anxiety for wealth in all things; then you will drive the multitude of thoughts into captivity, when you do not give the heart to the cares of material things; then also you will carry the cross undistracted (Matt 16:24), when you deny the desire to acquire, but the thought of material things will predict old age to you, and diseases, so that it may divide your hope toward God by money.
